m.howTo: Press your lips together and hum. Hold it: mmm.

mouth.text: Lips together. Hum through your nose. Voice on.

a.howTo: Open wide, as if to bite an apple. Say aaa as in apple.

mouth.text: Open your mouth wide, with your jaw down. Keep your tongue low and flat. Voice on.

s.howTo: Teeth close together, push air out like a snake. Hold it: sss.

mouth.text: Teeth close together. Tongue behind your teeth. Blow a thin stream of air. Voice off.

i.howTo: Say iii as in igloo. Keep your mouth small and relaxed.

mouth.text: Keep your mouth small and relaxed. Tongue a little forward. Voice on.

t.howTo: Tap the tip of your tongue just behind your top teeth. Short and crisp: t-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Touch your tongue tip just behind your top teeth. Let out a quick puff of air. Voice off.

p.howTo: Close your lips, then let out a tiny puff of air. Short: p-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Lips together, then open them with a quick puff of air. Voice off.

f.howTo: Rest your top teeth on your bottom lip and blow. Hold it: fff. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Top teeth on your bottom lip. Blow air out. Voice off.

o.howTo: Say ooo as in octopus. Open your mouth wide and round.

mouth.text: Open your mouth wide and round, like an O. Keep your tongue low and still. Voice on.

n.howTo: Put your tongue behind your top teeth and hum through your nose. Hold it: nnn. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Tongue behind your top teeth. Hum through your nose. Voice on.

d.howTo: Tap your tongue behind your top teeth and let your voice out. Short: d-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Tap your tongue behind your top teeth, quick and light. Voice on.

c.howTo: Lift the back of your tongue, then let it drop with a puff of air. Short: k-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Lift the back of your tongue to the roof of your mouth. Drop it with a quick puff of air. Voice off.

h.howTo: Breathe out as if fogging a mirror. Short: h-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Open your mouth a little. Breathe out, as if fogging a mirror. Voice off.

u.howTo: Say uuu as in umbrella. Keep your mouth relaxed and open a little.

mouth.text: Open your mouth a little. Keep your jaw and tongue relaxed and low. Voice on.

g.howTo: Lift the back of your tongue and let your voice out. Short: g-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Lift the back of your tongue to the roof of your mouth. Let it drop quickly. Voice on.

l.howTo: Put the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth. Say lion but stop before ion: l-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Touch your tongue tip behind your top teeth. Let the sound flow around it. Voice on.

r.howTo: Pull your tongue back and let your voice hum. Hold it: rrr. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Pull your tongue back and up, without touching the roof. Round your lips a little. Voice on.

b.howTo: Close your lips, then let your voice pop out. Short: b-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Lips together, then pop them open. Voice on.

e.howTo: Say eee as in egg. Open your mouth a little, wider than for iii.
e.parentNote: Let your child say the i sound first (iii as in igloo). Then compare pin and pen: which one has the new sound? Later, bit and bet.

mouth.text: Open your mouth a little, a bit wider than for i. Keep your tongue forward and relaxed. Voice on.

j.howTo: Let the sound pop out with your lips a little round. Short: j-. Do not add uh.

mouth.text: Round your lips a little. Press your tongue up, then let the sound burst out. Voice on.

w.howTo: Round your lips, then open them quickly. Short: w-. Do not add uh.
w.parentNote: The name of the letter w does not have its sound in it, so this lesson has one extra game. Say the sound, w-, not the letter name.

mouth.text: Round your lips like a small O, then open them quickly. Voice on.

v.howTo: Rest your top teeth on your bottom lip, like f, and turn your voice on. Hold it: vvv. Do not add uh.
v.parentNote: The sound vvv is the buzzing partner of fff. Let your child say fff first, then vvv, with a hand on the throat. Then compare fan and van.

mouth.text: Top teeth on your bottom lip, like f. Now turn your voice on and feel the buzz. Voice on.

y.howTo: Smile a little and lift the middle of your tongue, then glide down. Short: y-. Do not add uh.
y.parentNote: The name of the letter y starts with a different sound. Say the sound, y-, not the letter name. Compare yet and wet: which one starts with y-?

mouth.text: Smile a little. Lift the middle of your tongue, then let it glide down. Voice on.

z.howTo: Close your teeth, like s, and turn your voice on. Hold it: zzz. Do not add uh.
z.parentNote: The sound zzz is the buzzing partner of sss. Let your child say sss first, then zzz, with a hand on the throat.

mouth.text: Teeth close together, like s. Now turn your voice on and feel the buzz. Voice on.

x.howTo: x is two quick sounds, k and s, said together. Short: ks-. It comes at the end of a word.
x.parentNote: The letter x comes at the end of words. Say fox, six and box slowly, and let your child listen for the last sound.

mouth.text: Two quick sounds: tap the back of your tongue up (k), then blow air through your teeth (s). Voice off.

q.howTo: q always comes with u. Together they say kw-, quickly, as one sound.
q.parentNote: The letter q is always followed by u. Treat qu as one unit. Together they say kw-.

mouth.text: Lift the back of your tongue (k), then round your lips (w). Say both quickly as one sound. Voice on.

sh.howTo: Say shhh as in ship, like asking for quiet. Hold it: shhh.
sh.parentNote: Two letters, one sound. Slide under both letters at once: shhh. Compare sip and ship: which one has the new sound?

mouth.text: Round your lips a little and close your teeth. Blow a long stream of air. Voice off.

ch.howTo: Say ch- as in chip, like a quick sneeze. Short: ch-. Do not add uh.
ch.parentNote: Two letters, one sound. Say ch- like a quick sneeze, not chuh. Compare ship and chip: which one starts with the new sound?

mouth.text: Round your lips, then let a quick burst of air out through your teeth, like a sneeze. Voice off.

th.howTo: Say th- as in thin: poke your tongue out between your teeth and blow. Do not add uh.
th.parentNote: The letters th make two sounds, with the tongue between the teeth for both. Put a hand on your throat. In that it buzzes (thhh). In thin it does not (th-). Say both and feel the difference. Quiet th is easy to mix up with f: compare fin and thin.

mouth.text: Poke your tongue tip out between your teeth and blow air, as in thin. Voice off.

ck.howTo: ck says k-, the same sound as c and k. It comes right after a short vowel at the end of a word.
ck.parentNote: Two letters, one sound: ck says k- and comes at the end of a short word, like back and duck. Slide under both letters at once.

mouth.text: Lift the back of your tongue, then drop it with a quick puff of air, like c and k. Voice off.

ff.howTo: Two of the same letter say the same sound as one: ff says fff, ll says l-, ss says sss, zz says zzz.
ff.parentNote: Doubled letters come right after a short vowel at the end of a short word: puff, bell, miss, buzz. Two letters, one sound: the same sound the single letter makes. Slide under both letters at once.

mouth.text: Two letters, one sound, the same as the single letter. Say it once: top teeth on your bottom lip for ff. Voice off.

wh.howTo: wh says w-, the same sound as w. Round your lips, then open them quickly. Do not add uh.
wh.parentNote: The letters wh say the same sound as w. Slide under both letters at once. Compare wig and whip: which one has the new letters?

mouth.text: Round your lips like a small O, then open them quickly, just like w. Voice on.

ng.howTo: ng is one sound at the end of a word, like the end of sing. Hum through your nose with the back of your tongue up.
ng.parentNote: The letters ng are taught as chunks: -ang, -ing, -ong, -ung. The vowel sounds a little different before ng, so read the whole chunk: rang, sing, long, hung.

mouth.text: Lift the back of your tongue to the roof of your mouth and hum through your nose. Voice on.

nk.howTo: nk is n, then a quick k, at the end of a word, like the end of bank. Back of your tongue up, then a puff.
nk.parentNote: The letters nk are taught as chunks: -ank, -ink, -onk, -unk. Read the whole chunk: bank, pink, honk, junk.

mouth.text: Lift the back of your tongue and hum through your nose, then end with a quick puff, like k. Voice on.

st.howTo: Say the s and the t as one smooth glide: ssst-. Keep the s going, then tap the t. Do not add uh between them.
st.parentNote: A blend is two sounds said close together. Each letter keeps its own sound: s says sss and t says t-. At the end of a word the s and t glide together: last, nest, soft, gift.

mouth.text: Hold the s: teeth together, thin air. Then tap your tongue behind your top teeth for t. Glide. Voice off.

nd.howTo: Say the n or m and then the d, p or t straight after it, no uh between. The n or m melts into the vowel, so listen for it.
nd.parentNote: The n or m in nd, mp and nt melts into the vowel, so it is easy to leave out: sad becomes sand, cap becomes camp. Say the word slowly and let your child hear the nnn or mmm before the last sound. The next stop, Tricky Sounds, practices exactly this.

mouth.text: Hum the n or m, tongue up behind your top teeth. Then tap out d, p or t. The hum melts into the vowel. Voice on.

sp.howTo: Hold the s and slide straight into the next sound: sssp-. Do not say suh-p. st works the same way: ssstop.
sp.parentNote: Hold the s, then slide into the next sound: sssp-in, not suh-pin. The pair st from lesson 34 now comes at the start of words too: stop, step. Chains add a missing sound to make a new word: top, stop.

mouth.text: Hold the s, then slide straight into p (lips pop) or k (back of the tongue). Glide, no uh. Voice off.

sn.howTo: Hold the s and slide into the next sound: sssnnn. Do not say suh-n. The same for sw, sm and sl.
sn.parentNote: Four more s-blends: sn, sw, sm, sl. Hold the s, then slide into the next sound. Try a chain: sap, snap; lip, slip; wing, swing.

mouth.text: Hold the s, then slide into n or m (hum), w (round lips) or l (tongue up). Glide, no uh. Voice on.

bl.howTo: Glide the first sound straight into l: bl-, cl-, fl-. Say block, not buh-lock.
bl.parentNote: The l-blends: bl, cl, fl. Glide the first sound straight into l: block, not buh-lock. Keep it quick and smooth.

mouth.text: Say the first sound and glide straight into l, tongue behind your top teeth. Quick, no uh. Voice on.

pl.howTo: Glide the first sound straight into l: pl-, gl-. Say plan, not puh-lan.
pl.parentNote: Two more l-blends: pl and gl. Glide into l: plan, not puh-lan; glad, not guh-lad.

mouth.text: Pop the p or g and glide straight into l, tongue behind your top teeth. No uh. Voice on.

br.howTo: Glide the first sound straight into r: br-, tr-, cr-. Say brush, not buh-rush.
br.parentNote: The r-blends start here: br, tr, cr. Glide into r. Note that tr often sounds close to chr (trip) and that is normal speech.

mouth.text: Say the first sound and glide straight into r, tongue pulled back. Quick, no uh. Voice on.

dr.howTo: Glide the first sound straight into r: dr-, fr-, gr-. Say drum, not duh-rum.
dr.parentNote: The last r-blends: dr, fr, gr. Glide into r. Note that dr often sounds close to jr (drip) and that is normal speech.

mouth.text: Say d, f or g and glide straight into r, tongue pulled back. No uh. Voice on.

mix.howTo: Blends can come at the start of a word, at the end, or both: stamp, crust, plant. Glide each pair, with no uh.
mix.parentNote: The longest short-vowel words yet: stamp, crust, blend, frost, plant (five sounds each). Let your child slide under the whole word, gliding each blend. crash, flesh and think mix blends with digraphs.

mouth.text: Glide each pair, at the start, the end, or both: stamp. Keep every letter sound, no uh. Voice on.

checkpoints.line: Two sounds that are easy to mix up: mmm and nnn. Let's listen closely.
checkpoints.end: Great listening! Your child can tell mmm from nnn.

checkpoints.title: Tricky Sounds
checkpoints.hint: Breathe it out, like fogging a mirror: h-. No 'huh.'
checkpoints.line: Easy to miss: the breath sound h-. A word can start with it or not, like hat and at. Let's listen closely.

my.tricky: The letter y says long i here.

said.tricky: The letters ai say short e here.

does.tricky: The letters oe say short u and the letter s says "z" here.
